items.title: 8.3 Production and detection of plane polarized light

source_refs.note: Topic 8.3 with Fig. 8.5 and the Ponder Upon box (PDF 176-177, printed 173-174).

blocks.text: The light emitted by an ordinary incandescent bulb, and also by the Sun, is unpolarized, because its electrical vibrations are randomly oriented in space (Fig. 8.5a).

If unpolarized light is made incident on a sheet of polaroid (the polarizer), the transmitted light will be plane polarized. If a second sheet of polaroid is placed so that the axes of the two polaroids, shown by straight lines drawn on them, are parallel (Fig. 8.5b), the light is transmitted through the second polaroid. If the second polaroid (the analyzer) is slowly rotated about the beam of light as the axis of rotation, the light emerging from the second polaroid gets dimmer and dimmer and disappears when the axes become mutually perpendicular. The light reappears on further rotation and becomes brightest when the axes are again parallel to each other.

blocks.alt: Two rows. Unpolarized light, vibrating in all directions, passes a polarizer and comes out vibrating in one plane. (a) With the analyzer's axis parallel to the polarizer's, the light passes and the screen is lit. (b) With the analyzer turned through 90 degrees, no light gets through and the screen is dark, showing that light waves are transverse.
blocks.caption: Polarizer and analyzer with parallel (a) and crossed (b) axes: light waves are transverse (original diagram after Figure 8.5).

blocks.title: What the experiment proves
blocks.text: This experiment proves that light waves are transverse waves. If the light waves were longitudinal, they would never disappear, even if the two polaroids were mutually perpendicular.
Light reflected from the smooth surface of water is partially polarized parallel to the surface (Ponder Upon).

blocks.prompt: When unpolarized light of intensity I0 falls on a polarizing sheet, what intensity is not transmitted (numerical 8.1)? Would it be possible to use a polarizer as an analyzer (constructed response 8.2)?
blocks.explanation: A polarizer passes only the component of the vibrations along its axis, which for unpolarized light is half the intensity, so I0/2 is transmitted and I0/2 is not transmitted. Yes: polarizer and analyzer are identical polaroid sheets, and the name depends only on their position. In Fig. 8.5 the second polaroid is used as an analyzer, and a polaroid sheet or a pair of polarized sunglasses rotated in front of light reflected from water or from a table acts as an analyzer, showing that this light is partly polarized.

items: Light from a bulb or the Sun is unpolarized. Polarizer: makes plane polarized light. Analyzer: a second polaroid; parallel axes pass the light, rotating it dims the light, crossed axes stop it, parallel again brightest.
This proves light is transverse: a longitudinal wave would never disappear between crossed polaroids.
